Yeah, those MB Steampunk pens are pretty neat.

For inks, it's such a personal thing that I hesitate to make any recommendations other than "try a lot of inks". Did your pen come with a converter? If so, buy a bunch of samples from Goulet and see what you like before you buy full bottles (If you don't have a converter you can buy one there too). I, (and probably most users) are on a quest to find "the ink" and favorites change often.

Pens < $100: Lots of options.

  • You can find used Lamy 2000s for that price (great for your first gold nib).
  • Lamy Studio
  • Almost all Monteverde pens.
  • Many Conklin offerings
  • Anything from TWSBI
  • Sheaffer 100
  • Pelikan M200 (the other pen in my Lamy 2000 pic)
  • A lot of vintage pens.
  • The obligatory Lamy Safari/Al-star

There are a ton more options too. I own or have owned all of the pens that I listed and they are all great in that price point. I would suggest looking around, finding something that you like, then posting here and in other forums for opinions.

That is really cool. I will start doing some research and see. Since you said you owned all of them, which is the thickest in the body? I love my Cross but it does feel a bit thin. I was thinking for my next I would go larger. My Cross did not come with a converter (on my get list). Is there a recommendation on those you could through my way or advice on purchasing one before I go do m research?

Order is body thickness, large to small.

The Al-Star, TWSBI, and Conklin AA are all pretty similar in diameter and are pretty thick without being "oversized", next are the Lamy Studio and 2k (and probably the Monteverdes depending on which one you are looking at), then the Pelikan, and finally the Sheaffer. I'm having a hard time finding a measurement on your pen, but from my experience with Cross, I would imagine that it fits somewhere around the Pelikan.

Keep in mind though, that for comfort, the size of the grip section is more important than body thickness usually.

For converters: Cross has a proprietary cartridge size, so unfortunatly you have to by converter specifically for Cross pens. So, you it looks like you only have one option (shame, because they're a little pricey). Be careful because it looks like they have one specifically for the Townsend and one for everything else. This looks like your guy. You might find it a bit cheaper onAamazon, but if you plan to order some ink samples from Goulet anyway, the savings in shipping will probably outweigh any savings in product cost. Plus, Goulet is great to the community and I try to support them even if I can find an item cheaper on Amazon.

The constitutional right is for closely held businesses to refuse to pay for birth control. Under this new rule, those closely held businesses are still not required to pay.

The Obama administration on Friday issued its final rules for employers who morally object to covering birth control in their health insurance plans. The accommodation ensures that all employed women, unless they work for a place of worship, will still have their birth control covered at no cost to them, even if their employers refuse to cover it.

Under the new rule, a closely held for-profit company that objects to covering contraception in its health plan can write a letter to the Department of Health and Human Services stating its objection. HHS will then notify a third-party insurer of the company's objection, and the insurer will provide birth control coverage to the company's female employees at no additional cost to the company.
